differences.what: wall head: the heavy bracketed cornice over the front at about 7.9 m (the camera's own height reading); the build's walls stood 0.7 m higher

north pavilion: the north part of the front proud, its south side face shaded, round-headed windows in both storeys under moulded hoods, rising past the main cornice; the build's front is flat there and carries a two-storey canted bay
bay window: a one-storey bay on the south part with pilaster strips and its own cornice; built by T-2408 as the 1874 engraving's hooded canted bay, its cornice under the hood

entrance: the stoop rising straight from the gate (x 93-140 px, about v 6.3-7.5 at the street line) to a door beside the pavilion's south face. Built (T-2409): the door moved to v 6.6, its 1.8 m stoop rising straight to it and its landing ending at the pavilion's south face; the porch before the pavilion stands behind the sketch's lattice fence and its '1620' cartouche hides the door's hood
fence: a lattice of interlaced arches between square piers with capped tops, on a base, gate piers at the walk; the build's is iron rails on a stone curb with urned piers
the roof: the panel cuts the house at the cornice
colour and walling: a pen sketch
